IncidentBot: ALERT: P1 - widespread TLS handshake failures in us-east-1 impacting /v1/chat and /v1/generate. Incident INC-2026-79 created. Paging: @nora (oncall). Start: 2450000123.

Nora (oncall): ack. I'm seeing 525 and 526 spike in the gateway. Console says TLS handshake failure rate 58% in us-east-1. Standby while I gather proxy logs.

MonitoringBot: Metric breach: tls_handshake_errors > 800/min across prod-gateway cluster. Top symptom: "TLS alert" and "ssl3_get_record:wrong version number" in client side logs.

Dev (eng-sre): joining. Any recent infra ops or cert rotations? Any peering changes?

OpsBot: Recent automation events: cert-rotation batch #CR-582 triggered at 22:10:10 UTC (target: edge proxies). Peering preference change applied by netops at 22:09:50 UTC to route via transit-b path. No code deploys in last 3 hours.

Nora (oncall): pasting logs from a handful of failing proxies: ```2026-05-02T22:11:34Z proxy[sidecar-04]: WARN tls: handshake failure from 10.18.9.77:53412 -> 10.22.3.9:443; alert 40``` ```2026-05-02T22:11:35Z haproxy[frontend]: SSL handshake error: short read during handshake``` Also ran `openssl s_client -connect prod-api.use1.internal:443 -servername prod.api` and got: ```CONNECTED(00000003)
write:errno=1041408102
140810810371200:error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:155
---
no peer certificate available
---```

Omar (net-eng): netops seeing elevated ICMP "fragmentation needed" messages on peered link between us-east-core and us-east-inference. Peering vendor maintenance log shows transit-b applied MTU clamp at 22:08 UTC. Could be PMTU/DF causing TLS ClientHello fragmentation and drop.

Lina (support): customer impact: several PLG customers reporting failed API calls and spikes in 5xx. Opened high-priority tickets and posted a banner. I'll update customers: ETA 20m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Dev (eng-sre): hypothesis list: H1: MTU reduction on new peering path led to fragmentation of ClientHello (SNI/ALPN/OCSP size) causing handshake failures. H2: partial cert-rotation left mixed cert chains on proxies causing "unknown authority" on some paths. H3: TLS library/alg mismatch introduced by new certs. Prioritize network since fragmentation will affect most flows.

Nora (oncall): running `ip link show` and `ip route get` on affected host: local mtu 1500 but traceroute shows hop with MTU=1400. I'm starting a tcpdump: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 host 10.22.3.9 and port 443 -w /tmp/tls_frag.pcap`

Dev (eng-sre): please also collect `openssl s_client -connect` output from inside the mesh and from a client simulator outside the VPC to see if behaviour differs. Also paste the cert serials on proxies: `openssl x509 -in /etc/ssl/proxy.pem -noout -serial`

Nora (oncall): attaching quick outputs: cert serials: many proxies still show old serial 0x7D2F, ~40% show new serial 0x8E4B. Openssl from inside mesh: completes but returns cert chain length mismatch on some nodes. From public client sim: sees "unexpected record".

Omar (net-eng): tcpdump + tshark quick check: I see repeated ICMP "Fragmentation needed; DF set" packets and ClientHello bytes not reaching server fully. pcap capture saved to incident board. Also seeing a spike in TCP retransmits and occasional RSTs.

Dev (eng-sre): mapping evidence: H1 supported by ICMP frag-needed, pcap missing full ClientHello; H2 supported by cert serial mismatch and some x509 verify failures observed in proxy logs. Both seem to be happening concurrently. Need to mitigate quickly.

Nora (oncall): proposed mitigations: A) rollback peering preference to route via legacy path (restore MTU >=1500) to immediately stop fragmentation; B) pause/rollback cert-rotation to ensure uniform cert chains; C) temporarily disable OCSP stapling and advertise TLS1.2 fallback to reduce ClientHello size. Which to do first?

Omar (net-eng): network rollback first (fastest broad effect). I'll change route preference to prefer direct-core path now. ETA ~60-90s to converge. Monitoring net metrics after change.

MonitoringBot: Netops event logged: peering preference reverted at 2450000255. Observed decrease in ICMP frag-needed messages immediately.

Nora (oncall): after rollback: error rate dropped from 58% to 9% within 90s. Some customers still see failures likely from cert mismatches.

Lina (support): posting update to customers: "Partial resolution: network route restored and a large majority of requests are succeeding. We continue to investigate cert rotation impact. Full RCA to follow." :white_check_mark:

Dev (eng-sre): running cert consistency check across proxies and rolling back new certs on nodes that failed chain verification. Command used: `for h in $(cat proxy_hosts.txt); do ssh $h 'openssl x509 -noout -serial -in /etc/ssl/proxy.pem'; done` then orchestration rollback job. I'll run `openssl verify -CAfile /etc/ssl/ca-bundle.pem /etc/ssl/proxy.pem` after rollback.

Nora (oncall): cert rollback started. Verifying nodes as they come up: after rollback all proxies report old serial and openssl verify passes. Post-rollback logs no longer show x509 errors. Error rate now <1%.

Dev (eng-sre): attaching artifacts for RCA: `tls_frag.pcap`, `proxy-handshake-22-11.log`, `route-change-audit.log`, transit vendor maintenance ticket TKT-2026-99, openssl s_client outputs. Compiling timeline and hypothesis notes.

Omar (net-eng): root cause notes: transit-b applied MTU-reducing policy during maintenance. Our peering preference change sent TLS-heavy flows over that path with DF set causing fragmentation/ICMP drop. Simultaneously, an automated cert rotation partially rolled out leaving mixed cert chains on some proxies. The intersection of both issues amplified customer impact.

Dev (eng-sre): timeline draft: - 22:08:00 UTC: transit-b MTU clamp applied (vendor maintenance) - 22:09:50 UTC: peering pref change routes traffic via transit-b - 22:10:10 UTC: automated cert rotation triggered (partial application) - 22:11:20 UTC: TLS handshake errors spike - 22:13:00 UTC: network route rollback initiated - 22:14:30 UTC: cert rollback started - 22:25:00 UTC: error rate <1% and incident stabilized

Lina (support): customer impact summary for postmortem: ~14 orgs impacted, peak failure rate ~62% on /v1 endpoints, estimated 1.1M failed requests during 17-minute window, top 5 customers got fallback behavior; support escalations opened.

Dev (eng-sre): hypotheses tracked in-thread: H1 (primary): PMTU/fragmentation causing ClientHello drop 1 supported by ICMP and pcap. H2 (contributor): partial cert rotation causing x509 chain errors 1 supported by serial mismatch and verify failures fixed by rollback. H3 (unlikely): cipher policy mismatch - no clear evidence.

Omar (net-eng): immediate action items: - Add PMTU/MTU path checks + alerting for TLS service routes (owner: net-eng) - Gate routing changes if path MTU < 1500 (owner: netops) - Add automated PMTU verification in routing change playbooks and block risky peering preferences (owner: infra-automation)

Dev (eng-sre): infra action items: - Add cert-rotation canary that verifies full chain across all proxy pools before marking job successful (owner: infra-deploy) - Add a rollback-on-failure step for cert jobs (owner: infra-deploy) - Add monitoring for mixed cert serials across proxies (owner: infra-monitoring)

Lina (support): customer follow-ups: I'll prepare customer-facing RCA draft once postmortem is posted. Notifying account teams for top impacted tenants.

Nora (oncall): handoff: I'm handing to @dev for postmortem write-up. I'll be available for 30m on pager. Thanks all. :wave:

MonitoringBot: Incident RESOLVED at 2450000450. Postmortem assigned to @dev.

Dev (eng-sre): final summary for thread: Root cause = combination of transit MTU reduction + routing change exposing PMTU issue + partial cert rotation. Immediate mitigations = route rollback + cert rollback. Long-term fixes: PMTU automation, routing MTU checks, cert-rotation gating and mixed-serial alerts. Will author full RCA doc in /docs/incidents/INC-2026-79 with attached evidence.
